entries.answer: Think of a snapshot when a teammate plays the ball. In the opponents’ half, a player is in an offside position if their head, body or feet are nearer the goal than both the ball and the second-last opponent. Level is onside; hands and arms do not count. Being ahead alone is not an offence: they must join the play, for example by receiving the pass or interfering with an opponent. There is no offside directly from a goal kick, throw-in or corner. This diagram explains the rule, not a verdict on this match.
